about.title: Personal Injury Help in Pasadena, California
about.longDescription: Pasadena moves at its own pace. Commuters funnel onto the I-210 Foothill Freeway each morning, Colorado Boulevard carries shoppers and Rose Parade crowds through Old Pasadena, and Fair Oaks Avenue and Orange Grove Boulevard stitch the neighborhoods together. In 2025, the most recent finalized year of public records, the city logged 922 injury collisions. Those crashes left 1,333 people hurt and took 4 lives. Reports tend to cluster on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., when the week's last commute overlaps with the start of the weekend. Behind each of those numbers is someone sorting out medical bills, missed shifts, and an insurance adjuster who calls before the bruises fade. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims for people in Pasadena and across Los Angeles County. Our team works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you were hit while crossing Colorado near Old Pasadena, rear-ended on the 210, or hurt on someone else's property, one conversation can help clarify your options.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Pasadena Claim

items.title: Two years is the usual window
items.desc: California gives most injury claims two years from the date of harm to file in court. Waiting too long can close the door entirely, so early questions matter.

items.title: Shorter deadlines for public agencies
items.desc: If a city bus, a Caltrans-maintained stretch of the 210, or another government entity is involved, you may have as little as six months to file a formal claim. Knowing who is responsible early protects your timeline.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame, your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it is not wiped out.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and there is no attorney fee unless money is recovered for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Pasadena?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. If a government entity is involved, a formal claim may need to be filed within six months. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to ask early rather than assume there is time.

items.question: Where do crashes in Pasadena tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along the I-210 Foothill Freeway, Fair Oaks Avenue, Orange Grove Boulevard, and Colorado Boulevard. In 2025, the city recorded 922 injury collisions, with reports peaking on Fridays from roughly 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. These are simply the corridors that carry the most traffic and generate the most reports.

items.question: What if the other driver says I caused the collision?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means partial responsibility reduces what you can recover but does not bar you from recovering anything. We can review the police report, witness statements, and any camera footage to sort out how fault should actually be divided.

items.question: Who will handle my case?
items.answer: You will work directly with a personal injury attorney. We handle your case from start to finish, and there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Any fee arrangement is spelled out in writing before you agree to anything.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with our team?
items.answer: There is no charge to contact us. We take injury cases on contingency, so you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. Any fee arrangement is spelled out in writing before you agree to anything.
